items.title: Explain why SHD does not reproduce (ours 37.5, published 33.5)
items.criterion: A definition or data difference identified that accounts for the gap, or a documented reason it cannot be settled
items.note: Not settleable from public data. The authors' baseline code orients undecided CPDAG edges lower index -> higher ('liberal', TabCausal run_pc.py) and counts a reversal once; under that rule our SHD is 35.43 (within 2.81 of 33.52) but F1 0.396 (published 0.333, tolerance 0.045); under random orientation F1 matches and SHD does not. The published means also cover 50 unreleased scenarios. The paper's appendix B (which states the rule) could not be read.

items.title: Replay sampler: which declared interventions are interventions in name only
items.criterion: For every declared intervention in the replay sampler's data, whether the target's distribution moves (KS, Holm 1%); the in-name-only count reported
items.note: On the released obs+int files (produced by the same generator spec the replay sampler executes): no detectable shift in the target or any child for 252 of 945 declared interventions (semantic) and 1,354 of 1,520 (formula), KS with Holm at 1%. About 28 intervened rows per target, so shifts below roughly KS D 0.4 go undetected: 'no detectable effect', not proof of none. Most targets are roots (655 / 1,200), resampled per the release's semantics.
